# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 72/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72.

Every rule could be decided from the code. The main gaps are a missing `lang` attribute, no `Sitemap:` line in `robots.txt`, canonicals missing on two pages, a Blog page that only fills in after JavaScript runs, and a Pricing page marked noindex even though your sitemap lists it. These results are read from code, not measured on a live site.

I sampled 5 routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs`, `/blog` and `/thank-you`. I left `/thank-you` out of the route-based rules because it is deliberately noindex and appears in neither the sitemap nor the navigation. I read `geo.config.json`, which allows AI search crawlers and blocks training crawlers.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Add a `Sitemap:` line to robots.txt
- **Why it matters:** a sitemap is your list of pages. Crawlers look in `robots.txt` to find it, and yours doesn't point to it.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` (the file has no `Sitemap:` line, while `public/sitemap.xml` exists)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 80 (from 72)

### 2. Set the page language on `<html>`
- **Why it matters:** the `lang` attribute tells machines and screen readers which language the site is in. Your config says `en`, but the layout doesn't set it. Every page is affected.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 80 (from 72)

### 3. Add canonical links to `/docs` and `/blog`
- **Why it matters:** a canonical link names the main address of a page. Home and Pricing have one, but Docs and Blog don't, so search engines have to guess.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` and `app/blog/page.tsx` (this page has no metadata at all, so it also has no title or description)
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 76 (from 72)

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |

| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. 3 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Problem | Not run | `app/docs/page.tsx:1` has none, and `app/blog/page.tsx` has none. 2 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:8` `fetch('/api/posts')` inside `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line. The sitemap itself is valid. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11` `<html>` with no `lang`. This affects all routes. |
| GEO-016 | Pages are reachable by normal links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13` plain `<a href>` links in the nav |

## Other problems found

- **Pricing is in the sitemap but marked noindex.** `public/sitemap.xml:4` `<loc>https://www.ledger.example/pricing</loc>` conflicts with `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. This sends mixed signals, and Pricing also has a canonical. Fix: remove the `robots` setting if you want it found, or take it out of the sitemap if you don't.
- **Blog posts come from `/api/posts`, and the repository has no such route.** `app/blog/page.tsx:8` `fetch('/api/posts')`. I can't tell from the code where the posts come from.

## Worth considering

- **Give each blog post its own page.** `app/blog/page.tsx:10`: `posts.map((p) => <article key={p.id}>{p.title}</article>)`. Posts show only a title and have no address of their own, so they can't be linked, shared or listed in the sitemap.
- **Say what the plans cost.** `app/pricing/page.tsx:4`: `Free for up to three people.` This is the only pricing fact, and it's the first thing a visitor would ask about. Paid tiers, if any, could be written out as text.
- **Expand the Docs page.** `app/docs/page.tsx:4`: `Start by importing your bank feed.` The page names a first step and stops, so a reader gets nothing about what comes next.
- **Label the business with structured data.** `app/layout.tsx:5`: `title: 'Ledger: accounting for small teams'`. The site's name and what it does are visible on the page. Organization or `SoftwareApplication` JSON-LD could label them for machines.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Blog content:** whether `/api/posts` returns data, and what the Blog page looks like to a crawler without JavaScript. A live scan would confirm it.
- **Canonical and sitemap targets:** whether they answer 200 on the live site (live only).

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site. `geo.config.json` confirms it with `aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
- Blocking GPTBot and `/thank-you` being noindex are deliberate choices, so I haven't counted them.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
